title: Shared Email Domain, Two Real Companies
scenario_text: Kvarken Cloud (a SaaS vendor) runs a lead-to-account matching job in Salesforce and its dedupe rule proposes merging two accounts at 0.91 confidence because both use email addresses at the domain grptech.io. Account A-1201 is "Grimsby Robotics Inc." (EIN 27-5561120, D-U-N-S 08-114-9921, HQ desk in Austin, industry: industrial automation, ARR $180,000, contacts ada@grptech.io, sam@grptech.io). Account A-1330 is "Grimsby Ventures LLC" (EIN 46-8890457, DUNS 08-114-9945, HQ desk in Boston, industry: venture capital, ARR $54,000, contact partner@grptech.io). Both use grptech.io because a shared holding-group IT team provisions email for several unrelated portfolio companies under one vanity domain; the domain's WHOIS lists "GRP Technology Services," a managed-IT provider, as registrant. The two companies have different EINs, different DUNS, different industries, different HQ states, and different billing contacts and contracts. There is no parent/subsidiary linkage in D&B between them; GRP Technology Services is only a shared IT vendor. A sales ops analyst is about to approve the merge on the strength of the matching domain and similar name stem "Grimsby." The analyst also observes that a handful of other accounts in the same territory share grptech.io addresses, all provisioned by the same managed-IT team, which suggests the domain is a recurring source of false matches rather than a reliable identity key for any single customer.
question: Should the two accounts be merged, and why?
choices: Yes, merge them, because a shared email domain plus a common name stem reliably indicates one company operating two divisions.
No, keep them separate; the shared domain is a managed-IT vanity domain, and the distinct EINs, DUNS, industries, and contracts show two unrelated legal entities.
Yes, merge them under Grimsby Ventures LLC, since a venture firm is presumptively the parent of a similarly named operating company.
No, but only because their ARR figures differ; if the revenue matched they would be the same account.
